title: Satellite-image clustering guides discovery of four late Miocene fossil sites in Mozambique’s Urema Rift
summary: Unsupervised k-means clustering of seven Landsat 8 spectral bands highlighted a small set of priority areas for paleontological field survey in Gorongosa National Park. The 2018 campaign documented four new late Miocene fossil localities; three lay within the model’s target cluster and the fourth was less than 90 m away in the same gully system. Together, the sites expose the first reported estuarine coastal-forest fossil setting in the East African Rift System, filling a regional paleoenvironmental gap.
ai_technology: Unsupervised k-means clustering of Landsat 8 imagery
organization: University of Oxford; University of Coimbra; University of North Carolina at Greensboro; University of Algarve; Gorongosa National Park

evidence.tested: Unsupervised k-means clustering of seven Landsat 8 spectral bands highlighted a small set of priority areas for paleontological field survey in Gorongosa National Park.
evidence.unknown: This was a pilot study in a 36 km² area and the model had notable false positives: reported precision was 55.56%, despite 84.6% overall accuracy. Three of four new localities overlapped the selected cluster; the fourth was less than 90 m away and was found by surveying the same gully system, so model localization for that site is indirect. The findings are four new fossil localities, not four new hominin taxa; the reported estuarine coastal-forest interpretation is a paleoenvironmental inference.
evidence.ai_role: The authors clustered seven spectral bands without pre-labeled land-cover classes, compared clusters with known fossil localities, and selected the cluster containing most known sites as a predictive target for field prospecting. This decision-support workflow directed the 2018 field survey that documented the new localities; a random forest was separately used to estimate spectral-band importance.
